headline: This law lets the independent insurance expert on the Financial Stability Oversight Council keep serving after a six-year term ends if no successor has been confirmed yet.
what_it_does: It changes the Financial Stability Act of 2010 so the council's independent member with insurance expertise can stay on past the end of the six-year term if the president has not named a successor in time. The member may serve until 18 months after the term ends or until a successor is confirmed, whichever comes first.

who_it_affects.group: The independent member of the Financial Stability Oversight Council with insurance expertise
who_it_affects.how: This member can keep serving for a limited time after the six-year term ends if a replacement has not been named.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 27, 2017; the summary does not describe a separate effective date.
